subject: HorizonAI: elevated 5xx/429 spikes and retry storm — remediation & makeup proposal
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@horizonai.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Nina Rao <nina.operations@horizonai.com>, Legal <legal@horizonai.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: elevated 5xx/429 spikes causing customer failures — immediate remediation requested

SoojIN — (cc'ing our ops and legal)

We experienced a ~45-minute window of elevated 5xx and 429 responses yesterday morning (peak between 07:30–08:15 PST) which cascaded into a retry storm on our side and caused failed critical inference calls for several production customers. Attached a sample log slice and our internal request traces. Impact: ~12% of production traffic hit failures, several downstream jobs timed out and retried aggressively. This directly affected revenue for two customers and triggered their incident policies.

We need three things ASAP:
- Immediate mitigation steps you can apply today to stabilize (rate-limiting, fallback routing to model-variant, temporary throttles)
- An initial RCA and estimated timeline for a full postmortem
- A proposal for makeup credits for the affected billing period (we will escalate to procurement/legal if we don't get a concrete offer within 72 hours)

Please treat this as urgent — our CTO is asking for an executive update in the morning.

Attachments: [attachment: horizon_error_log_20261112.log (1.1 MB)]

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Platform Engineering
HorizonAI
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@horizonai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: elevated 5xx/429 spikes causing customer failures — immediate remediation requested

Samir — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I'm really sorry for the disruption. We've prioritized this and I've looped in ops and the account team. Immediate actions we are pushing now:

1) Rolling an emergency routing change to divert traffic from the stressed cluster to a warm standby model-variant (ongoing, expect stabilization within 15–30 minutes).
2) Applying temporary per-customer soft-rate limits to suppress retry amplification while we stabilize upstream autoscaling.
3) Enabling extra KV-cache retention for in-flight sessions to reduce repeated generation load.

Hannah — can you run an initial telemetry pass and reply with the root-correlated signals (autoscaler events, model rollout IDs, token latencies)? Lauren — I'll coordinate credits and commercial messaging with you. Rishi — can you prep a short exec brief for our CSM/Rev Ops to share with their CTO?

We will follow up with a proposed makeup credit framework within 48 hours and the preliminary RCA within 72 hours. I understand the sensitivity — I'm escalating to our head of SRE now.

— Soojin
SoojIN Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: elevated 5xx/429 spikes causing customer failures — initial telemetry notes

Quick notes from ops (initial, not the full RCA):
- Time window confirmed: 07:22–08:07 PST
- Error profile: 60% 5xx (503/502), 40% 429s. Elevated p95/p99 generation latencies preceding spikes.
- Correlated signal: a model variant rollout started at 07:12 which increased average token compute by ~18% for that cluster. Autoscaler reacted but initial cooldown and scale-up lag created contention on a subset of GPUs -> backlog -> request timeouts -> client retries -> retry amplification.
- Observed throttle: our fallback policy wasn't triggered because the rollout used a non-compatible variant tag, so automatic fallback routing didn't engage.

Immediate ops recommendation implemented: divert to warm pool + enforce short client-side retry window. We'll capture detailed traces and provide artifact by EOD.

I'll attach an incident summary draft and a proposed credit calc we can use as a starting point.

Attachments: [attachment: incident_summary_draft.pdf], [attachment: proposed_credit_calc.xlsx]

- Hannah
Head of SRE Operations
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@horizonai.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Legal <legal@horizonai.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposal: makeup credit + short-term safeguards (HorizonAI incident)

Samir — appreciate the quick sync yesterday. Based on preliminary telemetry and the impact window, here's a commercial proposal we hope is reasonable to resolve this quickly and avoid escalation: 

1) Makeup credit: Redwood proposes a one-time credit equal to 25% of your monthly invoiced usage for the service window impacted (we can apply a prorated credit if you'd prefer exact usage-window calc). We included the proposed_credit_calc.xlsx with both approaches.
2) Operational remediation: priority postmortem + action items (we'll share the full RCA within 4 business days).
3) Preventive commitment: a free 30-day trial of Dedicated warm capacity for the critical customer routes (to isolate you from noisy multi-tenant bursts) and priority capacity provisioning on request for the next 90 days.

If this is acceptable, Legal can accept a short amendment and we'll apply the credit to your next invoice and fast-track the Dedicated trial. We want to make this right promptly.

Please let us know if you'd prefer a different makeup calculation (percentage vs. dollar cap).

— Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Legal <legal@horizonai.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@horizonai.com>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: makeup credit + short-term safeguards (HorizonAI incident)

Lauren / Soojin — we discussed internally and HorizonAI is prepared to accept Redwood's proposal with a minor contractual amendment to document the credit and the Dedicated trial. Please prepare the amendment for signature and include: exact credit amount (prorated to affected window using attached calc), timeline for RCA delivery (no later than 4 business days from acceptance), and confirmation of the Dedicated trial start date.

We are also requesting one additional item: a clause committing Redwood to a rollback/hold policy for model rollouts impacting production (a 24-hour hold if a new variant causes >5% error increase). We can sign on receipt of the short amendment via DocuSign.

Looking forward to the incident postmortem link and the implemented safeguards.

— Horizon Legal
(internal note appended by lauren_bishop@redwood.com)

Action items:
- Hannah to finalize RCA and postmortem doc and publish to: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/HZ-20261112-postmortem by 2026-11-16 EOD.
- Soojin to confirm the exact prorated credit amount using the proposed_credit_calc.xlsx and send the amendment to Horizon Legal.
- Rishi to draft an exec summary for our CEO/COO for transparency.
- Ops to add the 24-hour rollback/hold policy to the rollout playbook and schedule a review with Horizon ops.

DocuSign link will be generated by RevOps after we lock numbers. Planned customer-facing resolution timeline: credit applied to next invoice; Dedicated trial start within 7 calendar days of signed amendment.
